key_insight: FracGen learns fracture dynamics from a single intact image by conditioning video generation on physics signals, enabling controllable tearing and deformation without per-scene simulation at test time.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical way to synthesize physically plausible fracture videos for design, testing, and analysis of brittle or deformable materials with less reliance on expensive experimental capture or simulation.
method: Builds FracSim, an MPM-based fracture simulation pipeline with a continuum damage model to generate paired fracture videos and dense physical fields.
Trains FracGen to jointly predict RGB video and physics maps, so the model learns physical state rather than only appearance.
Uses physics-informed losses to enforce consistency among predicted fracture, deformation, and damage fields.
evidence_signal: The paper reports a new benchmark for physical plausibility and states that FracGen outperforms prior video generation baselines in both visual fidelity and physical fidelity.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and realism of the simulated supervision, so domain gaps between FracSim and real materials may limit generalization.
paper_title: FracGen: Learning How Objects Stretch and Tear with Physics-Informed Video Generation
